questions.question: On a 1:25,000 OS map, two points are 7.2 cm apart. What is the actual distance between them in kilometres?
questions.correctAnswer: Actual distance = map distance × scale = 7.2 cm × 25,000 = 180,000 cm = 1,800 m = 1.8 km.

questions.question: Describe the contour pattern you would expect to see for (a) a steep slope, (b) a valley, (c) a summit.
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Steep slope: contour lines very close together, indicating height increases rapidly over a short distance. (b) Valley: V-shaped contour lines pointing uphill (towards higher ground), with the river flowing along the valley floor away from the point of the V. questions.question: A river drops 150 metres over a horizontal distance of 3 km. Calculate the gradient as a ratio.
questions.correctAnswer: Gradient = VI ÷ HE = 150 m ÷ 3,000 m = 150/3000 = 1/20 or 1:20. This means for every 20 metres horizontally, the land rises 1 metre vertically.

questions.question: Explain what vertical exaggeration is and why it is used in cross-sections.
questions.correctAnswer: Vertical exaggeration is when the vertical scale of a cross-section is larger (shows more detail) than the horizontal scale, making slopes appear steeper than they really are. It is used because real landscapes often have gentle slopes that would appear almost flat if drawn at true scale. questions.question: What is a bearing and how is it different from a compass direction?
questions.correctAnswer: A bearing is a precise angle measured clockwise from north (0-360°), expressed as a 3-digit number (e.g. 045°, 270°). A compass direction is an approximate direction using cardinal and intercardinal points (N, NE, E, etc.). A bearing is more precise - "NE" could mean anything from 022° to 068°, while a bearing of 045° is exact.
